plan_title: Oxy Wasson San Andres Field Amended Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The combined boundary of the Denver, Willard, Wasson ODC and Bennett Ranch units plus a half-mile buffer (p21).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the four unit boundaries plus a half-mile buffer, since the stabilized plume is expected to stay inside the field (p22).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores and surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, third-party drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated negligible or low (p23-28).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline (CO2 flooding began in 1983). The baseline is existing automated operational data (injection set points and flags, production forecasts, inspection work orders, H2S alarms) used to flag excursions (p35-36).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report, filed around March 31 with other GHG reports, with the mass balance and estimated leakage; well changes noted in the annual report; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data (p5, p28, p35-36, p40, p42-43).

rows.detail: Seven custody transfer meters on CO2 received from the Permian Basin pipeline system plus outlet meters at three CO2 recovery plants and the Bennett Ranch reinjection facility; CO2 concentration at least quarterly.
rows.location: Pipeline delivery points (M1, M2, M10, M11, M13, M14, M20); recovery plant outlets (M3, M12, M15, M19)
rows.evidence_quote: These meters measure flow rate continually.

rows.detail: Injection plans programmed into WAG skids; pressure monitors flag statistically significant deviations; SCADA monitors wellhead pressure; WAG skids shut off automatically above programmed pressure.
rows.location: Each injection well and WAG skid
rows.trigger_or_response: Flagged excursion: field personnel investigate, work order if unresolved, screened for leakage; pressure above programmed level triggers automatic shutoff.
rows.evidence_quote: Pressure in injection wells is monitored on a continual basis.

rows.detail: Annular pressure in wellheads monitored to detect tubing and casing leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly: inspect; repair with materials on hand, otherwise shut in and work order; workover crew within days.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads

rows.detail: MITs on injectors listed in the response table for tubing and casing leaks; no interval given.
rows.trigger_or_response: Tubing or casing leak: well shut in and workover crew responds within days.

rows.detail: Each producer tested about every two months at satellites (8-12 hours); produced gas metered at plant outlets and sampled at least quarterly for CO2; performance compared with forecast.
rows.location: Each production well; satellites; recovery plant outlets
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from forecast: well management personnel investigate; work order; leakage quantified by material balance if found.
rows.evidence_quote: each well being tested approximately once every two months

rows.detail: Reservoir pressure routinely measured for modeling and operations; response table relies on pressure at WAG headers and high pressure in new wells. No observation wells or gauges named.
rows.location: WAG headers; newly drilled wells (no observation wells named)
rows.trigger_or_response: High pressure: re-enter and reseal abandoned wells, manage fluids along lease lines, keep below parting pressure, or shut in injectors near a seismic event.
rows.evidence_quote: The reservoir pressure in the WSA is collected for use in reservoir modeling and operations management.

rows.detail: Routine field visits to wells and surface facilities looking for white CO2 clouds and ice; also used to spot unapproved drilling.
rows.location: Field-wide wells, satellites, tank batteries, pipelines
rows.trigger_or_response: Problem found: investigate, work order tracked to completion, leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Field inspections are conducted on a routine basis by field personnel.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors (alarm at 10 ppm); H2S is used as a proxy for CO2 leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, investigate source, work order, quantify CO2 for the annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: H2S monitors are worn by all field personnel.

rows.detail: Oxy participates in TexNet and says it will keep monitoring for seismic signals; also a one-time 2022 review of the USGS catalog (M3.0+). No site seismometers.
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismic event: shut in injectors near the event, assess the reservoir and respond if needed.
rows.evidence_quote: will continue to monitor for seismic signals that could indicate the creation of potential leakage pathways in WSA.

rows.detail: Existing 3D seismic interpreted to rule out faults in the storage and confining zones; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy has analyzed 3D seismic data acquired over the WSA to assess potential leakage pathways.

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors used to estimate CO2 from surface equipment leaks and vents, reconciled with event-driven leak estimates to avoid double counting.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy uses 40 CFR Part §98 Subpart W to estimate the mass of CO2 emitted from surface equipment leaks and vented emissions at WSA.

rows.detail: Personnel watch the pipeline system through SCADA to detect and stop pipeline leaks; SCADA data also used to estimate leak duration and size.
rows.trigger_or_response: Pipeline leak detected: mitigate promptly and quantify under Subpart W.
rows.evidence_quote: Personnel continuously monitor the pipeline system using the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system

rows.detail: History-matched compositional reservoir simulation model used to confirm plume containment and forecast pressure decline to support a future request to stop reporting.
rows.trigger_or_response: Model results that change the MMA lead to a revised MRV plan.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy will use the history matched reservoir simulation model of the current WSA CO2 injection (see Section 3.5) to confirm CO2 plume containment.

rows.detail: Step-rate tests measure formation parting pressure so injection pressure can be kept below it.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection pressure is also maintained below the FPP (FPP is measured using step rate tests).

notes: The file for this slug is Oxy's July 2023 amended Wasson San Andres Field plan, which folds the Denver Unit's December 2015 plan into one plan covering the Denver, Willard, Wasson ODC and Bennett Ranch units. Production tests run about every two months; coded periodic_unspecified because the vocabulary has no bimonthly value. Table 2 lists five 'MON TEMP' monitoring wells, none active (4 plugged, 1 temporarily abandoned), and the plan gives them no monitoring role (p14). The plan says H2S in the injected gas is below the analyzer's detection threshold (p35), which limits the H2S-as-proxy approach; unlike the CapturePoint plans, no permanent H2S detectors are described. Reservoir pressure is said to be measured but no instruments or wells are named. Figures and maps are images. Pages 46-160 are the well list.
